access.edition_or_version: First edition, Methuen (London) / E. P. Dutton (US), 14 October 1926

mechanics.premise: Ten self-contained stories about a teddy bear and his friends in an invented woodland, presented by a narrator telling them to a child.
mechanics.point_of_view: Third-person narrator who addresses the child reader directly and co-plays the stories.
mechanics.invented_world_and_props: A small, self-contained woodland populated by invented creatures whose behaviour is internally consistent, functioning as props the reader imagines into.
mechanics.play_frame: Each episode is framed as a story being told, so impossible or absurd events are enjoyed without being treated as falsehoods.
mechanics.psychic_distance: A mock-naive, wide-eyed stance that renders the ordinary as gently strange rather than ironic.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Light, readable prose; invented creatures and neologisms; understatement; comic misapprehension played straight.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Gentle puzzle or mishap -> comic complication -> warm resolution; the register stays affectionate throughout.
mechanics.dialogue: Domestic, childlike exchanges whose humour comes from literal-minded misunderstanding rather than punchlines.
mechanics.conventions: Established the twentieth-century children's fantasy of an isolated, habitable invented world.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Sustains delight in invention with almost no appeal to danger or moral; later critics debate whether its remoteness is a humane refuge or an evasion of weight.
mechanics.critical_reception: Commercial and critical success on publication (150,000 copies that year); later readings range from Edenic Arcadia to feminist critique of its gender representation.
mechanics.audience_reception: Enduring global classic; adapted widely, including an authorized 2022 US public-domain entry.
